Phase I review · Data processing & visualisation

Rebuilding the AutoVLA data layer

AutoVLA turns driving into next-token prediction: a 5-second trajectory becomes ten discrete action tokens that a vision-language model emits in the same stream as its reasoning. This is the pipeline that produces those tokens — built, measured against the paper, and running end to end.

01

What the pipeline does

Raw driving logs become chat records. Along the way the ego trajectory is cut into half-second motion segments, those segments are clustered into a fixed vocabulary of physically feasible manoeuvres, and every training trajectory is rewritten as ten tokens drawn from that vocabulary.

The vocabulary is the point. Because each token is a real motion segment observed in a real log, a model that emits tokens cannot emit a trajectory the vehicle could not drive — the failure mode that sinks language models asked to produce raw waypoints.

Two more numbers line up with the paper's construction directly. The achieved covering radius is 0.063 m against the stated threshold of 0.05 m, and 99.9% of tokens survive inversion through a kinematic bicycle model — the dynamics check the project's fourth objective calls for.

The residual gap is expected: these numbers come from a procedural stand-in corpus rather than the Waymo motion dataset the paper clusters. Real logs are denser and more stereotyped, which is exactly what a nearest-neighbour codebook rewards. Swapping in nuScenes changes only the first stage.

03

One finding worth reporting

Where the paper is silent

The paper says only that each 0.5 s segment is mapped “to its nearest action token”. Which pose the segment is measured from turns out to decide the result, and it is not stated.

Measure each segment from the ground-truth pose and any heading quantisation error rotates every later waypoint; error compounds over the horizon. Measure it from the pose the decoder has actually reached and each token corrects its predecessor's drift.

Measured from ground truth
14.67 cm
final error far exceeds average
Measured from the reconstructed pose
2.40 cm
final error ≈ average

AutoVLA reports an FDE of 2.03 cm against an ADE of 1.82 cm. Final error sitting level with average error is the signature of the second scheme, so this is almost certainly what the paper does — and the naive reading of that one sentence costs a sixfold accuracy loss. Both are implemented.

05

Milestones

Milestones 1–3 rebuild the paper's data layer, 4–7 its model and training, and 8–11 add the uncertainty channel that AutoVLA does not have — the project's own contribution.

  • M0
    Environment and repo scaffold Done
    Package layout and a config in which every constant is traced to a line in the paper.
  • M1
    Unified sample schema DoneRaghul
    One record shape across nuPlan, nuScenes, Waymo and CARLA. The nuScenes adapter reads the JSON tables directly, so it needs no devkit; it is waiting only on the 4 GB mini download.
  • M2
    Physical action tokenizer DoneSahithya
    K-disk clustering into 2048 tokens, encode by contour distance, decode by SE(2) composition, every token validated against vehicle limits.
  • M3
    Statistics and visualisation Done
    The eight figures on this page, plus a text report regenerated on every run.
  • M4
    VLM backbone and action vocabulary NextSahithya · Raghul
    Qwen2.5-VL-3B, tokenizer extended with the 2048 <action_i> tokens already emitted by the pipeline, LoRA at rank 8, vision encoder frozen.
  • M5
    Chain-of-thought annotation PlannedSahithya
    Four-part reasoning per sample. DriveLM QA reformatted into that shape, with BDD-X for the explanation-quality benchmark, in place of the paper's 72B annotation run.
  • M6
    Supervised fine-tuning, fast and slow modes PlannedSahithya · Medha
    Language-modelling loss plus the auxiliary action loss, weighted up on samples that carry reasoning.
  • M7
    Open-loop evaluation PlannedSahithya
    L2 at 1/2/3 s and collision rate on nuScenes, plus the fast-versus-slow latency gap that motivates adaptive reasoning in the first place.
  • M8
    Bayesian uncertainty head PlannedRaghul
    Aleatoric via a log-variance branch, epistemic via MC dropout, fused into a confidence score and calibrated. Reported as expected calibration error and failure-prediction AUROC. This is the part that is genuinely new relative to AutoVLA.
  • M9
    Uncertainty-gated reasoning PlannedMedha
    Confidence, not a scenario heuristic, decides how much reasoning to spend — and when to fall back to a minimal-risk manoeuvre instead.
  • M10
    GRPO reinforcement fine-tuning PlannedMedha
    Group-relative advantage with a KL leash to the fine-tuned reference, driving reward minus a sigmoid penalty on reasoning length — extended with a calibration term that punishes confident-but-wrong actions.
  • M11
    Benchmarks, ablations, report PlannedAll
    Collision rate, L2, calibration error, AUROC, and the ablation on the calibration reward term.
06

Risks to settle early

Objective 1 is not in the base paper

AutoVLA has no bird's-eye-view transformer — camera frames go straight into the vision encoder. A BEVFormer-style backbone is an addition, and a large training job on its own. Either scope it down to a frozen pretrained encoder, or fold the effort into the uncertainty head. Worth raising with the guide, because it changes one member's workload substantially.

CARLA closed-loop will not run on this hardware

CARLA needs Linux or Windows with an NVIDIA GPU. Plan on the open-loop displacement reward the paper itself uses for Waymo, and treat live closed-loop rollout as a stretch goal contingent on lab access.

Fine-tuning needs a real GPU

A 3B vision-language model will not fine-tune usefully on a laptop. Budget Colab or Kaggle sessions and decide the dataset size before M4, since that decision sets how much of nuScenes to preprocess.

Fluent explanations are not faithful explanations

BLEU and CIDEr score wording against a reference, not whether the justification reflects what the policy actually did. If M5 lands early, add a counterfactual check — perturb the critical object and see whether the stated reason changes.

Every number on this page is regenerated by scripts/run_pipeline.py. Figures produced from the procedural corpus; the nuScenes adapter is written and waiting on the dataset download.
